anatomy.title: Anatomia
anatomy.item1: Alert — contêiner principal (<div role="alert">). Recebe a prop variant e qualquer atributo HTML de div.
anatomy.item2: AlertTitle — título do alerta (<h5>). Opcional, mas recomendado para leitores de tela.
anatomy.item3: AlertDescription — corpo de texto do alerta (<div>). Aceita parágrafos e conteúdo rico.
anatomy.item4: Ícone (opcional) — qualquer SVG como filho direto de Alert. Posicionado automaticamente à esquerda via CSS.
anatomy.structureCode:
<Alert variant="default">
  <Icon />           {/* ícone opcional — filho direto */}
  <AlertTitle />     {/* h5 — opcional mas recomendado */}
  <AlertDescription />{/* div — corpo do alerta */}
</Alert>

guidelines.title: 📋 Guidelines Obrigatórias
guidelines.item1: Use variant="default" para mensagens informativas e de sucesso.
guidelines.item2: Use variant="destructive" apenas para erros ou situações que requerem ação imediata.
guidelines.item3: Sempre forneça AlertTitle para contexto — leitores de tela anunciam o alerta com o título.
guidelines.item4: Não use Alert para mensagens temporárias (toasts) — use o componente Sonner.

do.title: Use quando
do.item1: O usuário precisa ser informado sobre o estado do sistema
do.item2: Uma ação resultou em erro e o usuário precisa saber o motivo
do.item3: Uma seção da página tem restrições ou condições especiais
do.item4: Um aviso de segurança ou dado sensível precisa de destaque

dont.title: Não use quando
dont.item3: Há muitos alertas na mesma página — revise o fluxo de UX

anatomy.title: Anatomy
anatomy.item1: Alert — root container (<div role="alert">). Accepts the variant prop and any div HTML attribute.
anatomy.item2: AlertTitle — alert title (<h5>). Optional but recommended for screen readers.
anatomy.item3: AlertDescription — alert body text (<div>). Accepts paragraphs and rich content.
anatomy.item4: Icon (optional) — any SVG as a direct child of Alert. Automatically positioned to the left via CSS.
anatomy.structureCode:
<Alert variant="default">
  <Icon />            {/* optional icon — direct child */}
  <AlertTitle />      {/* h5 — optional but recommended */}
  <AlertDescription />{/* div — alert body */}
</Alert>

guidelines.title: 📋 Required Guidelines
guidelines.item1: Use variant="default" for informational messages and success states.
guidelines.item2: Use variant="destructive" only for errors or situations requiring immediate action.
guidelines.item3: Always provide AlertTitle for context — screen readers announce the alert with the title.
guidelines.item4: Don't use Alert for temporary messages (toasts) — use the Sonner component.

do.title: Use when
do.item1: The user needs to be informed about system state
do.item2: An action resulted in an error and the user needs to know why
do.item3: A page section has special restrictions or conditions
do.item4: A security notice or sensitive data requires emphasis

dont.title: Don't use when
dont.item3: There are many alerts on the same page — review the UX flow

desc.format: Full sentence · neutral tone · include action when possible

pair1.do: Clear title + description with action instruction. Icon reinforces the message type.
pair1.dont: Alert without a title makes quick identification harder, especially for screen readers.

pair2.do: Destructive variant reserved for real errors that block the flow.
pair2.dont: Using destructive for informational warnings creates unnecessary anxiety.

accessibility.title: Accessibility
accessibility.summary: The Alert component uses role="alert" natively, which triggers automatic announcement by screen readers (implicit ARIA Live Region with aria-live="assertive"). Meets WCAG 2.1 level AA.
accessibility.item1: role="alert" — automatic announcement by assistive technologies when the alert is inserted into the DOM.
accessibility.item2: Contrast — destructive variant achieves ≥ 4.5:1 contrast between text and background in both light and dark modes.
accessibility.item3: Non-interactive — Alert does not receive focus; no specific keyboard navigation required.
accessibility.item4: AlertTitle required — provides semantic context; screen readers announce the title as part of the alert.

keyboard.tab: Not applicable — Alert is informational only, with no own focus.
keyboard.screenReader: Screen reader announces content automatically when the alert is inserted into the DOM.

sonner.name: Sonner (Toast)
sonner.desc: For temporary messages that disappear automatically.

alertDialog.name: AlertDialog
alertDialog.desc: For destructive action confirmations that require user response.

note1.title: role="alert" triggers screen readers immediately
note1.content: When an Alert is dynamically inserted into the DOM, screen readers like VoiceOver and NVDA announce the content immediately. Avoid rendering unnecessary alerts to not interrupt the user's flow.

note2.title: Icon positioned via absolute CSS
note2.content: The style [&>svg]:absolute [&>svg]:left-4 [&>svg]:top-4 positions any direct child SVG. Ensure the SVG has a defined size (e.g., h-4 w-4) to avoid out-of-proportion icons.
